audits.text:
## 3e0aef964b9e

**Classification: reproduced validation defect plus a concrete shortcut.**

I inspected the canonical donor geometry and 600 generated draws. Canonical donor connected-component sizes include isolated singletons in two examples and a four-cell 4-neighbor-connected vertical component in another. None of the 600 generated draws contained any 4-neighbor adjacency among donor cells (`checks/logs/adversarial-audit-probes.log`).

A concrete shortcut is: “move donor-colored pixels only when each donor is an isolated singleton; ignore connected donor components.” It fits the sampled generated curriculum but fails the canonical connected four-cell donor line.

I also directly called the generator’s `self_check` on the malformed two-color grid `[[0,1,0],[0,0,2],[0,0,0]]`, which has neither the required target structure nor a valid donor/hole relation. It returned `[]` (`checks/logs/adversarial-audit-probes.log`). That is a reproduced defect: the executable validator can accept an out-of-domain impostor.

**Recommended follow-up:** generate connected donor components with nonzero frequency, register an explicit witness/rival for component-preserving movement, and strengthen `self_check` to reconstruct and validate the target, holes, donor geometry, and expected count correspondence rather than checking only superficial grid properties.
